title: Add temporal-sigmoid-throttler and graceful cutover for bursty canary probes
author: Lena Zhang
release_notes: Introduce Temporal Sigmoid Throttler and Graceful Cutover to reduce false-positive canary regressions during traffic bursts. Smoother probe shaping and delayed final cutover lowers noisy rollbacks while preserving sensitivity to real regressions.
description:
Motivation: Canary evaluators are sensitive to short-lived traffic bursts that inflate tail latency and throughput variance, causing noisy false-positive rollbacks and developer friction. This PR implements a probe-rate controller (Temporal Sigmoid Throttler) that dynamically attenuates probe injection when burstiness and SLO gradient indicate transient noise, plus a Graceful Cutover policy that defers final traffic shifts until a stability window passes.

What this changes: Adds a probe rate controller that uses a short-term burst index, SLO gradient, and a configurable sigmoid shaping function to reduce probe intensity during high-variance windows; introduces a Graceful Cutover state machine in the rollout controller so final cutovers only occur after an adaptive stability score is met; expands metrics, traces, dashboards, and test harnesses.

Checklist: [x] Temporal Sigmoid algorithm implemented and unit-tested. [x] Integration tests exercising burst scenarios added. [x] Dashboards and alert rules updated. [x] Feature gated behind canary.temporal_sigmoid feature flag. [x] Rollout plan with progressive enablement prepared.

Why sigmoid shaping: A sigmoid curve provides a smooth attenuation factor between 0 and 1 as burst index increases, avoiding hard thresholds that cause oscillation. The shaping parameters are tunable per-customer workload profile.

Testing and results: Local load tests and perf lab synthetic traces (mixed steady+bursts) show false-positive canary triggers drop from ~14% to ~2% across 1-minute microburst scenarios, while detection latency for sustained regressions increases by <2s on average. E2E stability run on the perf-canary harness (100k synthetic requests over 60m with three injected regressions) passed without spurious rollbacks.

Rollout plan: Deploy to canary evaluator staging, enable feature flag at 10% of experiments for 48h, promote to 50% after automated regression-free window, and enable by default after one week with metric review. Built-in fallback: if stability score decays or new anomaly detectors fire, controller immediately reduces probe weight to zero and falls back to legacy probing.

Operational notes: New metrics emitted: canary.probe.attenuation, canary.stability_score, canary.burst_index, canary.cutover_state. Traces include probe.weight and cutover.decision_reason. Suggested SLO dashboards and alert thresholds included in docs.

Related: Linked Linear tickets ENG-10482 (canary instability), ENG-10490 (rollout guard improvements). Support ticket SUP-4482 documents a customer incident that motivated the approach.

Risks and mitigations: The main risk is over-attenuation delaying detection of real regressions during sustained low-signal periods; mitigated by conservative default sigmoid slope and a safety gate that forces evaluation when SLO degradation crosses a hard threshold.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the burst index calculation (prober_controller.py) and the stability score aggregation (slo/policies/graceful_cutover.policy). The feature flag and config schema live in infra/helm/canary-controller.yaml.

review_conversation: Diego Morales: Nice work. Two questions: how is burst_index calculated on multi-region traffic, and can we surface the attenuation factor in trace spans?
Lena Zhang: Burst index is a weighted percentile-based estimator that merges per-region indexes using recent qps weights; I added probe.weight to spans in the latest commit (d4c9a7f).
Aisha Patel: Integration tests look good, but add a test for sustained moderate load to ensure we don't delay detection longer than acceptable SLO window.
Lena Zhang: Added sustained-load scenario and updated the default sigmoid slope to be slightly steeper to reduce detection lag (commit f3e2b7c).
Marcus O'Neill: Approved. Please make sure runbooks and dashboard links are in the release notes.
CI: integration-e2e failed on first run due to a flake in the harness; rerun fixed it (see ci checks).
Release Manager: merged via squash after approvals and green CI.
summary_benchmarks: Synthetic 1-min microburst: false-positive canary triggers reduced from 14.2% -> 2.1%
Detection latency for sustained regressions increased by <2s on average at 95th percentile
E2E perf harness (60m, 3 injected regressions): no spurious rollbacks during burst windows
deployment_plan: Stage 1: Deploy to canary-evaluator staging cluster with feature flag off (smoke)
Stage 2: Enable feature flag at 10% of experiments for 48 hours; monitor canary.probe.attenuation and canary.stability_score
Stage 3: If metrics stable, increase to 50% experiments for 72 hours
Stage 4: Gradual enablement to 100% with weekly metric review and dashboards
Fallback: Feature flag off + probe weight forced to 0 if stability_score drops below threshold or another anomaly detector fires
